questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: What is the canonical standard form of a single-variable quadratic equation?

options.text: ax² + bx + c = 0 (where a ≠ 0)
ax + by + c = 0
ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0
y = mx + c

questions.explanation: A quadratic equation in standard form is written as ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, and c are real numbers and the leading coefficient a cannot equal 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: What is the discriminant formula for the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, and what does a negative discriminant indicate about its roots?

options.text: Δ = b² - 4ac; indicates two complex conjugate roots (no real roots)
Δ = b² + 4ac; indicates two distinct real roots
Δ = 4ac - b²; indicates one repeated real root
Δ = -b / (2a); indicates zero roots

questions.explanation: The discriminant is given by Δ = b² - 4ac. When Δ < 0, the square root involves an imaginary component, resulting in two distinct complex conjugate roots.

opt_2.explanation: The discriminant formula subtracts 4ac (b² - 4ac), not adds it.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Find the real solutions for the quadratic equation: x² - 5x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: Factoring x² - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0 yields x - 2 = 0 or x - 3 = 0, giving x = 2 and x = 3.

opt_2.explanation: Flipped the root signs; solving (x - a) = 0 results in x = +a.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: For the parabola described by y = a(x - h)² + k with a > 0, what are the coordinates of its minimum point?

options.text: (h, k)
(k, h)

questions.explanation: In vertex form y = a(x - h)² + k, the vertex is always located at (h, k). Since a > 0, the parabola opens upward and the vertex is the absolute minimum.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Which tree traversal order on a valid Binary Search Tree (BST) produces keys in strictly ascending sorted order?

options.text: In-order Traversal (Left, Root, Right)
Pre-order Traversal (Root, Left, Right)
Post-order Traversal (Left, Right, Root)
Level-order Traversal (Breadth First)

questions.explanation: Because every node in the left subtree is smaller than the root and every node in the right subtree is greater, visiting Left -> Root -> Right yields the natural ascending order.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching in an un-balanced (degenerate) Binary Search Tree versus an AVL-balanced BST?

options.text: Unbalanced: O(n), AVL Balanced: O(log n)
Unbalanced: O(log n), AVL Balanced: O(1)
Unbalanced: O(n²), AVL Balanced: O(n)
Both are always O(log n) regardless of balance

questions.explanation: An unbalanced BST can degenerate into a single linked list chain of height n, making search O(n). An AVL tree strictly enforces height balance h ≤ 1.44 log₂(n), guaranteeing O(log n) search.

opt_4.explanation: BSTs only achieve O(log n) when balanced; inserting sorted elements without self-balancing leads to O(n) degeneration.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: When deleting a node that possesses TWO children in a Binary Search Tree, what node should replace the deleted node to maintain the BST invariant?

options.text: Either Inorder Successor (min in right subtree) or Inorder Predecessor (max in left subtree)
The root of the entire tree
Any random leaf node in the tree
The immediate parent of the node

questions.explanation: The Inorder Successor (the minimum key in the right subtree) or Inorder Predecessor (maximum in left subtree) has at most one child and satisfies all BST ordering constraints when swapped.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Critique the AVL balance factor metric. Explain why Left-Right (LR) double rotations are necessary when an insertion occurs in the right subtree of the left child.
questions.correctAnswer: A single right rotation fails for LR cases because the inner grandchild remains deeper. An initial left rotation on the left child transforms LR into LL, allowing a subsequent right rotation to balance the root.
questions.explanation: In an LR imbalance, the center node is the tallest. A single rotation merely shifts the imbalance without reducing height. A double rotation (Left on child, then Right on root) properly elevates the center grandchild to the new subroot.
questions.sampleAnswer: In an LR imbalance (insertion into the right subtree of left child), a single right rotation does not reduce tree height because the deep node is on the inside branch. The left rotation first converts the subtree into a pure left-heavy (LL) form. The subsequent right rotation then promotes the balanced median element to the root, restoring balance factors to 0 or ±1.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Explain why a base case is strictly mandatory in any recursive algorithm, and what occurs at the machine runtime level if it is omitted.
questions.correctAnswer: A base case prevents infinite recursion and terminates execution. Without it, continuous activation frame allocations exhaust stack memory causing a stack overflow crash.
questions.explanation: Every recursive invocation allocates a new stack frame on the thread call stack. A base case terminates recursion; without it, stack capacity is exceeded causing stack overflow.
questions.sampleAnswer: A base case provides the termination condition that halts recursive branching. At the machine runtime level, every function invocation allocates a stack frame (activation record) on the call stack containing parameters, local variables, and return address. Without a base case, unbounded recursive calls continuously push new stack frames until call stack memory is exhausted, resulting in a fatal stack overflow runtime error.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: State the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) and describe the classic Square-Rectangle inheritance violation.
questions.correctAnswer: Subtypes must be substitutable for supertypes without altering correctness. Square inheriting from Rectangle violates LSP because setting width independently mutates height.
questions.explanation: LSP requires behavioral subtyping. Square inherits Rectangle width/height setters but couples them, breaking Rectangle client contracts.
questions.sampleAnswer: LSP requires that subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering program correctness. A Square inheriting from Rectangle breaks LSP because modifying width independently changes height, violating the Rectangle invariant.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff in supervised learning. How does model complexity influence both error components, and what technique prevents overfitting?
questions.correctAnswer: Bias arises from overly simplistic assumptions (underfitting) while variance arises from sensitivity to training noise (overfitting). Regularization and cross-validation optimize the tradeoff.
questions.explanation: Total generalization error = Bias² + Variance + Irreducible Error. High complexity reduces bias but increases variance.
questions.sampleAnswer: The bias-variance tradeoff decomposes total expected prediction error into squared bias, variance, and irreducible error. High bias models underfit by making overly simplistic assumptions, while high variance models overfit by modeling training noise. Increasing model complexity decreases bias but increases variance; optimal generalization occurs at the sweet spot minimizing their sum. Regularization (L1/L2) and cross-validation prevent overfitting.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Which graph traversal algorithm uses a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) Queue to explore vertices layer-by-layer in increasing order of distance?

options.text: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
Depth-First Search (DFS)
Topological Sort with Recursion Stack
Kruskal Minimum Spanning Tree

questions.explanation: Breadth-First Search (BFS) uses a FIFO queue to systematically visit all neighbor vertices at distance d before moving to distance d+1.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Why does Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm fail on graphs containing negative edge weights, whereas the Bellman-Ford algorithm handles them correctly?

options.text: Dijkstra greedily marks visited nodes as finalized assuming distances only increase; negative edges violate this monotonic property
Dijkstra uses O(V³) memory while Bellman-Ford uses O(1)
Bellman-Ford only works on unweighted trees
Dijkstra requires all vertices to have degree 2

questions.explanation: Dijkstra operates on the greedy invariant that once a vertex is extracted from the priority queue, its shortest path is settled. Negative edges can provide a cheaper detour later, breaking Dijkstra. Bellman-Ford relaxes all E edges V-1 times, accommodating negative weights.

opt_2.explanation: Space complexity is not the root cause; greedy monotonicity failure is the fundamental algorithmic breakdown.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What two fundamental characteristics must a computational problem exhibit for Dynamic Programming to be applicable and optimal?

options.text: Optimal Substructure and Overlapping Subproblems
Linear Time Complexity and Unsorted Data
Greedy Choice Property and Infinite Memory
Single Recursion Branch and Constant Space

questions.explanation: Optimal Substructure means an optimal solution to the problem contains optimal solutions to subproblems. Overlapping Subproblems means the same subproblems are solved repeatedly.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Given items with weights [1, 3, 4, 5] and values [1, 4, 5, 7], calculate the maximum value achievable in a knapsack with maximum weight capacity W = 7.

options.text: 9 (by taking items of weight 3 and 4 -> value 4 + 5 = 9)

questions.explanation: Testing combinations within capacity 7: {w:3, v:4} + {w:4, v:5} = weight 7, value 9. Other combinations: {w:1, v:1} + {w:5, v:7} = value 8. Max is 9.

opt_3.explanation: Value 11 exceeds the weight limit of 7 (weights 1+3+4 = 8 > 7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: What is the determinant of the 2x2 matrix A = [[3, 2], [1, 4]], and what does a non-zero determinant prove about the matrix?

options.text: det(A) = 10; proves the matrix is invertible (non-singular) with trivial kernel
det(A) = 14; proves the matrix has no eigenvalues
det(A) = 2; proves the matrix is orthogonal
det(A) = 0; proves the matrix is singular

questions.explanation: det(A) = (3)(4) - (2)(1) = 12 - 2 = 10. Since det(A) ≠ 0, A is invertible and its column vectors form a linearly independent basis for R².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Find the derivative of the function f(x) = x² · sin(x) with respect to x.

options.text: f'(x) = 2x sin(x) + x² cos(x)
f'(x) = 2x cos(x)
f'(x) = x² cos(x) - 2x sin(x)
f'(x) = 2x sin(x)

questions.explanation: By the Product Rule (u·v)' = u'v + uv': u = x² -> u' = 2x; v = sin(x) -> v' = cos(x). Thus f'(x) = 2x sin(x) + x² cos(x).

opt_2.explanation: Product rule was ignored; simply multiplied derivatives of each part (2x * cos(x)), which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Under what conditions is the matrix product AB = BA guaranteed for two n×n non-zero square matrices?

options.text: When A and B share a common eigenbasis or one is a scalar multiple of the identity matrix
For all symmetric square matrices of equal dimension
Whenever both determinants det(A) > 0 and det(B) > 0
Matrix multiplication is always commutative for square matrices

questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication is non-commutative in general. AB = BA only holds under specific conditions, such as when both matrices are simultaneously diagonalizable or when one is a scalar multiple of I.

opt_4.explanation: Confusing matrix algebra with scalar multiplication. In general, AB ≠ BA.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Compute the first derivative of the function f(x) = (3x² - 5)⁴ with respect to x.
questions.explanation: By the chain rule: d/dx [u⁴] = 4u³ · u'. Here u = 3x² - 5, so u' = 6x. Thus f'(x) = 4(3x² - 5)³ · (6x) = 24x(3x² - 5)³.

opt_2.explanation: Chain rule inner derivative omission: forgot to multiply by d/dx(3x² - 5) = 6x.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If event A and event B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3, what is P(A ∩ B) and are A and B independent?

options.text: P(A ∩ B) = 0; they are dependent events
P(A ∩ B) = 0.12; they are independent events
P(A ∩ B) = 0; they are independent events
P(A ∩ B) = 0.70; they are mutually dependent

questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive means they cannot co-occur, so P(A ∩ B) = 0. Since P(A) · P(B) = 0.12 ≠ 0, they violate independence. Knowing A occurred tells us B cannot occur!

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: What is the logical contrapositive of the conditional statement: "If an integer n is divisible by 4, then n is even"?

options.text: If n is odd, then n is not divisible by 4
If n is even, then n is divisible by 4
If n is not divisible by 4, then n is odd
n is divisible by 4 and n is odd

questions.explanation: The contrapositive of "P → Q" is "¬Q → ¬P". Here P: "n is divisible by 4", Q: "n is even". ¬Q: "n is odd", ¬P: "n is not divisible by 4".

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Under what condition does a square matrix A have an inverse A⁻¹?

options.text: The determinant det(A) ≠ 0 (matrix is non-singular)
All diagonal entries of A are non-zero
The matrix A must be symmetric
The trace of matrix A equals its dimension

questions.explanation: A matrix A is invertible if and only if it has full column rank, which is equivalent to det(A) ≠ 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Solve the separable differential equation dy/dx = 2xy with initial condition y(0) = 3.

options.text: y = 3e^(x²)
y = x² + 3
y = 2x² + 3

questions.explanation: Separating variables gives (1/y) dy = 2x dx. Integrating both sides: ln|y| = x² + C. Exponentiating: y = A e^(x²). Since y(0) = 3, A = 3, so y = 3e^(x²).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Determine if the vectors v₁ = (1, 0, 1), v₂ = (0, 1, 1), and v₃ = (1, 1, 2) in ℝ³ are linearly independent.

options.text: Linearly dependent, because v₃ = v₁ + v₂
Linearly independent, because all vectors are non-zero
Linearly independent, because their dot products are positive
Linearly dependent, because ℝ³ requires 4 vectors for a basis

questions.explanation: Notice that v₁ + v₂ = (1+0, 0+1, 1+1) = (1, 1, 2) = v₃. Since one vector is a non-trivial linear combination of the others, the set is linearly dependent.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is the mathematically proven information-theoretic lower bound for comparison-based sorting of n items in the worst case?

options.text: Ω(n log n)
Ω(n)
Ω(n²)
Ω(log n)

questions.explanation: There are n! possible permutations. Any comparison tree requires depth at least log₂(n!) = Ω(n log n) comparisons.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: In the classic Interval Scheduling problem, which greedy choice strategy provably yields the maximum number of mutually compatible intervals?

options.text: Select the interval that finishes earliest (Earliest Finish Time)
Select the interval that starts earliest (Earliest Start Time)
Select the interval with the shortest duration
Select the interval with the fewest conflicting overlaps

questions.explanation: Earliest Finish Time leaves the maximum available time remaining for subsequent intervals. A standard "greedy stays ahead" proof confirms optimality.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between Separate Chaining and Open Addressing for hash collision resolution?

options.text: Separate Chaining stores colliding keys in external linked buckets; Open Addressing probes alternative indices within the table array itself
Separate Chaining prevents all collisions, while Open Addressing causes infinite loops
Open Addressing requires twice as much memory per element as Separate Chaining
Separate Chaining only works with cryptographic hashes

questions.explanation: In Separate Chaining, buckets contain linked lists. In Open Addressing (Linear Probing, Quadratic, Double Hashing), all items reside directly inside the table array.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What constitutes a tail-recursive function, and why do modern compilers optimize it?

options.text: The recursive call is the very final operation executed, allowing the compiler to reuse the current stack frame (O(1) auxiliary stack space)
The function has two recursive calls placed in the middle of a loop
The function calls an external iterative loop upon termination
Tail recursion runs in O(0) time

questions.explanation: When no computation remains after the recursive invocation returns, the compiler can overwrite the caller's stack frame with the callee's arguments, transforming recursion into an efficient iterative jump.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: State the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) and describe the classic Square-Rectangle inheritance violation.
questions.correctAnswer: Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering program correctness. A Square inheriting from Rectangle breaks LSP if changing width modifies height unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: LSP states that objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without breaking application behavior. If Square inherits from Rectangle, setting width to 5 should not implicitly change height to 5 if client code expects independent width/height.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is a race condition in multi-threaded programming, and how does a Mutual Exclusion (Mutex) lock prevent it?
questions.correctAnswer: A race condition occurs when concurrent threads access shared mutable state without synchronization and the outcome depends on execution timing. A mutex ensures only one thread executes the critical section at a time.
questions.explanation: When two threads perform read-modify-write on shared variables simultaneously, intermediate writes can be lost. A mutex provides an atomic lock so that only the thread holding the lock can enter the critical section, serializing access to shared memory.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: Which loss function is standard for multi-class classification when model output layer uses Softmax activation?

options.text: Categorical Cross-Entropy Loss
Mean Squared Error (MSE)
Hinge Loss
Mean Absolute Percentage Error

questions.explanation: Cross-entropy loss measures the divergence between true one-hot labels and predicted probabilities from the Softmax distribution, penalizing confident wrong predictions exponentially.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: Why did the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function largely replace Sigmoid in deep hidden layers?

options.text: ReLU avoids the vanishing gradient problem for positive inputs (derivative is constant 1) and is computationally cheaper
ReLU bounds outputs strictly between -1 and 1
ReLU is completely differentiable everywhere including at x = 0
ReLU prevents neural networks from overfitting

questions.explanation: Sigmoid saturates at both tails with derivatives near zero (max derivative 0.25). Multiplying these across deep layers causes vanishing gradients. ReLU has derivative 1 for x > 0.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: Explain geometrically and mathematically why L1 regularization (Lasso) promotes sparsity by driving non-informative feature weights to exact zero, whereas L2 regularization (Ridge) does not.
questions.correctAnswer: L1 constraint contour is an L1 diamond with sharp corners on the coordinate axes. The loss ellipses touch the sharp corners where w_i = 0, zeroing out coefficients.
questions.explanation: L1 adds λ∑|w_i| to the loss, producing diamond-shaped constraint boundaries whose vertices align with the axes. The minimum of the objective frequently intersects these corners, setting weights to exactly 0. L2 adds λ∑w_i², creating spherical/circular contours that shrink weights toward zero without setting them to exact zero.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: In a medical cancer screening diagnostic system where catching every true positive case is critical, which evaluation metric should be maximized, and why?

options.text: Recall (Sensitivity), because false negatives must be minimized
Precision, because false positives are intolerable
Raw accuracy across the entire population
Specificity, to maximize healthy rejections

questions.explanation: Recall = TP / (TP + FN). In medical diagnostics, a False Negative (missing a sick patient) is life-threatening, so maximizing Recall is paramount.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: What is the primary advantage of Mini-batch Gradient Descent over both pure Batch Gradient Descent and pure Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)?

options.text: It leverages vectorized GPU hardware acceleration while maintaining stochastic noise to escape saddle points
It guarantees finding the global minimum for all non-convex loss surfaces
It eliminates the need to set or tune a learning rate parameter
It reduces the total number of epochs required to exactly one

questions.explanation: Mini-batch balances stability and computational speed. Matrix operations run efficiently on SIMD/GPU tensor cores, while batch stochasticity helps the optimizer escape local plateaus and saddle points.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: How does a Random Forest ensemble achieve lower variance than a single fully grown decision tree?
questions.correctAnswer: By averaging predictions of decorrelated trees trained on bootstrap samples with random feature subspace subsets (bagging + random feature selection).
questions.explanation: Single decision trees have high variance and overfit training noise. Random Forests use Bootstrap Aggregation (bagging) to sample training data with replacement and select a random subset of features (typically √m) at each split. This decorrelates the individual trees; averaging their predictions reduces overall variance by roughly 1/B.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: In Principal Component Analysis (PCA), what do the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the data covariance matrix represent?

options.text: Eigenvectors represent the orthogonal principal axes of maximum variance; eigenvalues quantify the variance explained along those axes
Eigenvectors represent class decision boundaries; eigenvalues represent misclassification rates
Eigenvectors are the original feature weights; eigenvalues represent L1 regularization penalties
Eigenvectors define the cluster centroids; eigenvalues define the radius of each cluster

questions.explanation: PCA computes the spectral decomposition of the covariance matrix Σ = VΛVᵀ. The eigenvectors define the orthogonal axes of variance, and the eigenvalues denote the magnitude of variance captured by each principal component.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the Inverse Document Frequency (IDF) weighting factor in the TF-IDF text representation scheme?

options.text: Downweight common words (like "the", "is") that appear across nearly all documents and upweight rare, domain-informative terms
Convert all uppercase letters to lowercase characters
Ensure every vector has unit Euclidean norm
Compute cosine similarity between two sentences directly

questions.explanation: TF alone assigns highest score to ubiquitous words. Multiplying by IDF = log(N / df) dampens words that appear everywhere, elevating distinctive keywords that distinguish document content.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Sum and Product of Roots (Vieta's Formulas)
questions.questionText: For the equation 2x² - 8x + 6 = 0, what are the sum and product of the roots according to Vieta's formulas?

options.text: Sum = 4, Product = 3
Sum = -4, Product = 3
Sum = 8, Product = 6
Sum = 2, Product = 6

questions.explanation: By Vieta's formulas, for ax² + bx + c = 0, sum of roots is -b/a = -(-8)/2 = 4, and product of roots is c/a = 6/2 = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If Q is an orthogonal matrix, which of the following properties must hold true?

options.text: QᵀQ = I and det(Q) = ±1
Q must be symmetric with det(Q) = 0
All eigenvalues of Q must equal 0
Q⁻¹ = -Q

questions.explanation: An orthogonal matrix satisfies Qᵀ = Q⁻¹, meaning QᵀQ = I. Taking the determinant yields (det Q)² = 1, so det(Q) = ±1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Evaluate the indefinite integral ∫ x · eˣ dx using integration by parts.

options.text: eˣ(x - 1) + C
x · eˣ + C
eˣ(x + 1) + C
½ x² · eˣ + C

questions.explanation: Let u = x (du = dx) and dv = eˣ dx (v = eˣ). By parts: ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du = x eˣ - ∫ eˣ dx = x eˣ - eˣ + C = eˣ(x - 1) + C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Evaluate the limit lim(x → 0) [sin(3x) / x] using derivatives or standard limits.

options.text: Does not exist

questions.explanation: Applying L'Hôpital's rule to the 0/0 indeterminate form: d/dx[sin(3x)] / d/dx[x] = 3 cos(3x) / 1. At x = 0, this evaluates to 3(1) = 3.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: In a Binary Search Tree, how is the in-order successor of a node with a non-empty right subtree identified?

options.text: The leftmost (minimum) node in its right subtree
The rightmost (maximum) node in its left subtree
Its immediate parent node
The root of the entire tree

questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits left, root, right. Thus the immediately next greater value after any node is the minimum element located in its right subtree, found by traversing left until null.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching in an un-balanced Binary Search Tree with N nodes?

options.text: O(N) when elements were inserted in sorted order forming a linked list
O(log N) under all insertion sequences
O(1) because pointers are followed directly
O(N²)

questions.explanation: If keys are inserted in sorted order without rebalancing, the BST degenerates into a linear chain (skewed tree) of height N, making search O(N).

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.subtopic: Topological Sort on Directed Acyclic Graphs
questions.questionText: Which graph property is strictly required in order for a valid topological ordering of vertices to exist?

options.text: The graph must be a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
The graph must be strongly connected and undirected
All edge weights must be strictly non-negative
The graph must contain an Eulerian circuit

questions.explanation: Topological sort linearizes dependencies such that for every directed edge u → v, u comes before v. A directed cycle makes this ordering impossible.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: Why would an engineer choose the Bellman-Ford algorithm over Dijkstra's algorithm for single-source shortest paths?

options.text: Bellman-Ford correctly handles negative edge weights and detects negative weight cycles
Bellman-Ford is asymptotically faster with O(V log V) complexity
Bellman-Ford only works on unweighted trees
Dijkstra requires the graph to have negative cycles

questions.explanation: Dijkstra greedily locks in visited node distances, failing when negative edge weights are present. Bellman-Ford relaxes all edges |V| - 1 times and can detect negative cycles.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: In the Longest Common Subsequence DP recurrence, what is the state transition when string characters s1[i] == s2[j]?

options.text: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]
dp[i][j] = 0

questions.explanation: When s1[i] == s2[j], both characters can be matched and appended to the optimal LCS of the prefixes of length i-1 and j-1, giving 1 + dp[i-1][j-1].

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: When optimizing the 0/1 Knapsack dynamic programming table from a 2D matrix dp[n][W] to a 1D array dp[W], how must the capacity loop iterate?

options.text: In reverse order (from W down to weight[i]) to prevent reusing the current item multiple times
In forward order (from weight[i] up to W)
In arbitrary order as addition is commutative
The 0/1 Knapsack problem cannot be space-optimized to 1D

questions.explanation: Iterating backwards ensures that when computing dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - weight[i]] + val[i]), the value dp[w - weight[i]] still represents state from the previous item (0/1 choice), not the current item (unbounded choice).

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: According to the Open/Closed Principle (the "O" in SOLID), software entities should be:

options.text: Open for extension, but closed for modification
Open source for public use, but closed for private use
Open to multiple inheritance, but closed to composition
Open to runtime mutation, but closed to static type checking

questions.explanation: The Open/Closed Principle states that classes should be design-extensible via inheritance or interfaces/strategies without modifying existing, tested source code.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is the primary architectural rationale behind the design maxim "Favor composition over inheritance"?

options.text: Composition reduces tight coupling and fragile base class hierarchies by composing behaviors dynamically at runtime
Inheritance consumes twice as much memory at runtime
Interfaces cannot be compiled in compiled languages
Composition prevents classes from using private methods

questions.explanation: Inheritance binds subclasses tightly to parent internal implementations (white-box reuse). Composition uses clean interfaces (black-box reuse), allowing behaviors to swap dynamically.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: For the divide-and-conquer recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n), what is the asymptotic runtime by the Master Theorem?

options.text: O(n log n)
O(n²)
O(n)
O(log n)

questions.explanation: Here a = 2, b = 2, so n^(log_b a) = n^(log_2 2) = n^1. Since the work per level f(n) = O(n) matches n^(log_b a), Master Theorem Case 2 applies: T(n) = O(n log n) (classic Merge Sort).

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: What is the load factor α of a hash table, and what action is triggered when α exceeds a defined threshold (e.g. 0.75)?

options.text: α = n / m (items / bucket capacity); exceeding the threshold triggers table resizing and rehashing of all elements to maintain O(1) average lookup
α is the memory consumed in bytes; exceeding the threshold halts the program
α is the count of duplicate keys allowed in the table
α is the number of hash functions applied per key

questions.explanation: The load factor α = n/m measures table fullness. As α grows, collisions multiply, causing operations to degrade towards O(n). Doubling capacity and rehashing restores expected O(1) time.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.questionText: When calculating the middle index in binary search on an array with large indices, why is `mid = low + (high - low) / 2` preferred over `mid = (low + high) / 2`?

options.text: It prevents integer 32-bit overflow when `low + high` exceeds 2³¹ - 1
It executes in fewer CPU machine cycles
It guarantees the mid index rounds up rather than down
It allows searching un-sorted arrays directly

questions.explanation: In languages with fixed-width integers, if low and high are both large positive integers, `low + high` can overflow into a negative integer, causing out-of-bounds exceptions.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: What is the primary advantage of k-fold cross-validation over a single fixed train/test split?

options.text: Every sample is used for both training and validation across folds, yielding a lower variance estimate of out-of-sample generalization error
It trains the model k times faster than a single split
It eliminates the need for testing data entirely
It automatically sets all model hyperparameters to their optimal values

questions.explanation: K-fold cross-validation partitions the dataset into k equal subsets, testing on each fold while training on the other k-1 folds. This reduces sampling bias and provides an honest performance estimate.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: In a medical cancer diagnostic screening system where missing a positive patient is catastrophic, which metric must be maximized as highest priority?

options.text: Recall (Sensitivity) to minimize False Negatives
Precision to minimize False Positives
Specificity only
Raw accuracy without class balancing

questions.explanation: Recall = TP / (TP + FN). When failing to detect a positive case (False Negative) has severe costs, maximizing Recall ensures nearly all true positive cases are flagged for clinical examination.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: Why do deep feedforward neural networks experience the vanishing gradient problem when using the standard Sigmoid activation function across many layers?

options.text: The maximum derivative of the sigmoid function is 0.25; by the chain rule, repeated multiplications cause gradients to decay exponentially toward zero in early layers
Sigmoid functions output negative values that cancel positive weights
The learning rate explodes to infinity in sigmoid backpropagation
Sigmoid activations cannot be computed on modern GPUs

questions.explanation: Since σ'(x) = σ(x)(1 - σ(x)) ≤ 0.25, multiplying many factors < 1 across 10+ layers during backpropagation causes ∂L/∂W in shallow layers to vanish, stalling parameter updates. ReLU mitigates this with a gradient of 1 for x > 0.

questions.subject: AI & Data Science
questions.questionText: How does a Random Forest ensemble reduce model variance compared to an individual deep decision tree?

options.text: By bootstrapping training samples and randomly subsetting candidate features at each split, then averaging decorrelated tree predictions
By pruning all leaf nodes until only the root split remains
By iteratively training trees on the residual errors of preceding trees
By enforcing strict linear boundaries across all dimensions

questions.explanation: Random Forest applies bagging (bootstrap aggregating) plus random feature subspace selection. Averaging B decorrelated trees reduces variance from σ² to (1 - ρ)σ²/B + ρσ², preventing overfitting.

teacherReviews.questionText: Critique the AVL balance factor metric. Explain why Left-Right (LR) double rotations are necessary when an insertion occurs in the right subtree of the left child.
teacherReviews.studentAnswerText: In an LR imbalance, the inserted node is in the inner grandchild position of the left child. A single right rotation fails because the deep node remains inside without reducing maximum height. We must first perform a left rotation on the left child to convert the LR imbalance into an LL form, followed by a right rotation on the root to elevate the median node to the subroot.
teacherReviews.rubricCriteria: balance factor, double rotation, left child, inner grandchild, LL transformation, height reduction

teacherReviews.questionText: Explain why a base case is strictly mandatory in any recursive algorithm, and what occurs at the machine runtime level if it is omitted.
teacherReviews.studentAnswerText: A base case is needed so the algorithm knows when to return. Without a base case, the computer keeps calling the function over and over until the program crashes.
teacherReviews.rubricCriteria: call stack, activation record, termination, stack overflow, base case, infinite recursion

teacherReviews.questionText: State the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) and describe the classic Square-Rectangle inheritance violation.
teacherReviews.studentAnswerText: LSP requires that subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering program correctness. A Square inheriting from Rectangle breaks LSP because modifying width independently changes height, violating the Rectangle invariant.
teacherReviews.rubricCriteria: substitutability, superclass, subclass, invariants, square rectangle, behavioral subtyping
teacherReviews.feedbackNotes: Excellent understanding of behavioral subtyping vs mathematical inheritance.

teacherReviews.questionText: Explain why Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm fails or produces incorrect results on graphs containing negative edge weights.
teacherReviews.studentAnswerText: Dijkstra greedily marks nodes as permanently visited assuming any newly discovered edge adds non-negative distance. A negative edge breaks this greedy invariant by potentially discovering shorter paths to already finalized nodes, leading to suboptimal paths.
teacherReviews.rubricCriteria: greedy invariant, non-negative weights, settled nodes, relaxation order, shortest path optimality
teacherReviews.feedbackNotes: Spot-on technical breakdown of the greedy invariant breakdown under negative weights.

teacherReviews.questionText: Compare top-down memoization with bottom-up tabulation in Dynamic Programming. Detail recursion overhead and state table transitions.
teacherReviews.studentAnswerText: Top-down memoization uses recursion to solve subproblems on demand, storing results in a hash table or array but incurring call-stack overhead. Tabulation is iterative, filling table entries from base cases up, preventing recursion depth limits and often enabling space optimization.
teacherReviews.rubricCriteria: memoization, tabulation, recursion stack, iterative, space optimization, state transitions
teacherReviews.feedbackNotes: Clear comparison of memory overhead and recursion limits.
